A1.justification: Both PDFs describe T3-S2S. All 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, CLIP scores and user ratings for 20 custom scenes, module and hyperparameter ablations, and appendix transfer experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on 50 custom scenes, an adapted T2I-CompBench evaluation, dense-tuning layer and cost experiments, and terrain-generation demonstrations.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds full-scene and empty-terrain generation branches connected by mask-guided feature sharing with a time-dependent blending schedule. This substantially extends the original single-image workflow. The core prompt-balancing and TopK feature-enhancement procedures remain unchanged despite renaming Characteristics Prominence to Characteristics Priority.

E1.justification: T2I-CompBench changes from a suggested benchmark in v1 to actual evaluation of color binding, spatial relations and small-object numeracy in v2. v2 also demonstrates paired isometric and terrain-only outputs. Non-game scenes and 3D reconstruction examples already existed in v1; those broad domains are not new.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds DenseDiff and T2I-Adapter to the custom-scene quantitative comparison; v1 included them only in qualitative comparisons. New Table 1 also includes Stable v3 and FLUX.1 reference scores, explicitly attributed to the benchmark source rather than newly run experiments. The original qualitative comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The reported custom evaluation expands from 20 to 50 scenes. v2 introduces GPT-4V-generated square sketches with manually adjusted sizes, B-VQA and UniDet metrics, and a stated 300-prompts-per-metric benchmark protocol. New layer-placement experiments measure memory and latency. Core inference settings remain unchanged. The numeracy passage's 100 examples and omitted minimum resolution leave that protocol incompletely specified.

E4.justification: New Appendix B, Table 3 and Figure 12 test where dense tuning should operate across ControlNet and U-Net, examining visual artifacts, accuracy, memory and latency. Figure 18 extends the hyperparameter analysis to additional scenes. The earlier TopK histogram, grayscale checks and model-transfer studies are retained; moving the histogram into Section 5.4 is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 newly states ten generated images per prompt for T2I-CompBench and explicitly labels three seed-specific examples in Figure 2. These are limited additions to sampling and seed disclosure, not evidence of increased repetitions for retained experiments. Neither version reports confidence intervals, dispersion estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Custom-scene scores change: T3-S2S global CLIP/user ratings move from 0.3497/3.88 in v1 Table 1 to 0.3491/3.79 in v2 Table 2, alongside the change from 20 to 50 scenes, so these are not same-setting performance comparisons. v2 adds T2I-CompBench results of 0.6872, 0.4256 and 0.6257 for color, spatial relations and numeracy, plus layer-cost measurements and terrain/3D outputs.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3 adds embedding-norm decomposition, bounds on projected key/value norms, and an approximate exponential attention-ratio derivation. These provide additional mathematical reasoning beyond v1's empirical motivation and standard attention equations, but do not constitute a new formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the central contribution from improved multi-instance sketch-to-image generation to controllable concept-art generation with paired isometric and terrain representations. Although v1 already illustrated downstream 3D reconstruction, the dual-representation terrain workflow becomes an explicit main contribution only in v2.

C2.justification: v2 explains the large-scene limitation through SDXL's 32-fold downsampling and adds segmentation/depth-estimation limitations for 3D assembly. Appendix B interprets layer-placement results through contour amplification and efficiency tradeoffs. The original energy-competition, noise, texture and base-model limitation discussions largely retain their meaning.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies expand-only self-attention modulation and the terrain-sharing parameters alpha=5 and gamma0=1. Appendix H substantially expands the previously brief 3D backend description with segmentation, heightmaps, texture and asset retrieval, and Unity assembly. Table 3 supplies memory and timing measurements, and the original code link is replaced by an official repository and maintained mirror.

R1.justification: v2 trims the broad text-to-image background citations and adds targeted foundations for its analysis and backend, including query-key normalization, SENet, Segment Anything, Osprey and 3D reconstruction methods. Its central positioning relative to ControlNet, Dense Diffusion, layout control and Sketch2Scene remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are reframed around concept-art and terrain generation. Section 3 is substantially rewritten and reorganized, method terminology changes, the overview structure is condensed, and the TopK appendix becomes Section 5.4. The limitations and backend descriptions are also extensively reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds the twin-branch diagram, benchmark and cost tables, layer-placement visualizations, and terrain columns in existing example grids. Attention/value visualizations gain annotations, main qualitative and ablation figures are rearranged into compact adjacent panels, and the 3D demonstrations are redesigned and expanded. These exceed simple renumbering or numerical table updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow quantitative validation through the compositional benchmark, direct quantitative DenseDiff/T2I-Adapter comparisons, and layer-placement/cost ablations. Expanded implementation and limitation discussions also make the design easier to assess. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: the numeracy setup is incomplete, Appendix E's six variants/120 sets are unreconciled with the expanded evaluation, and the new terrain branch receives qualitative rather than independent quantitative validation.
